about: Resources on the Pawnee language beyond the two books this project copies forms from. The fields before 'project' are copied from a catalogue the project's owner brought on 2026-11-15 (a spreadsheet kept out of git): its credibility scores and its notes are its compiler's judgement, made from web searches, and most archival items are described from their catalogue entries. Under 'project' stand this project's own decisions about each source. See sources/README.md and scripts/sources_catalogue.py.
spreadsheet_compiled: November 15, 2026, from web searches. Ratings are my judgment against the scale above.

records.title: Pawnee Nation Language Program (Cultural Resources Division)
records.creator: Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma
records.publisher: Pawnee Nation Cultural Resources Division, Pawnee, OK
records.contains: The tribe's own language program, housed with the THPO, NAGPRA office and Pawnee Nation Museum. Runs weekly community language and culture classes; announced online language classes (Mar 2025) and a Language & Culture class (Oct 2025).
records.why_rating: Tribal authority: the final word on current teaching, spelling and cultural protocol.
records.rights: Tribal materials; ask the program before reusing.

project.note: The Nation's 'Pawnee Language' page is https://pawneenation.org/pawnee-language/ and its Cultural Resources page https://pawneenation.org/cultural-resource-division/ (both answered on 2026-11-15).

checked.seen: Opened 2026-11-15: the Pawnee Nation's website, news under 'Language'. Posts: 'Online Language Classes Available' (14 March 2025), 'Language & Cultural Classes!' (25 March 2025), 'Pawnee Language & Culture Class' (6 October 2025). The site's own page 'Pawnee Language' (pawneenation.org/pawnee-language/) says 'Follow us on Facebook' and gives the language department's page.

project.title: The Pawnee Nation's language programme
project.says: The Nation's own programme, and the first place to ask. Its website announces language and culture classes; in March 2025 it announced online language classes. Ask the programme what is running now.

records.title: Pâripakûru' — Pawnee Language Department Facebook page
records.creator: Pawnee Nation Language Department
records.contains: The language department's own page (the “Pari Pakuru'” page). Class news, lessons and posts.
records.why_rating: Official program channel (identified as such by the San Juan College guide and by program teachers). Facebook blocks automated access, so individual posts were not reviewed.
records.rights: Posts belong to the Nation; ask before reuse.

project.title: The language department's Facebook page

records.creator: Pawnee Nation
records.contains: Recordings of the Nation's in-person community language classes.

records.rights: Tribe's content; link rather than re-host.

checked.seen: YouTube gives the playlist's title as 'Pawnee Language Classes' and its owner as 'The Pawnee Nation' (2026-11-15). The videos were not watched.

project.title: Recordings of the Nation's language classes

records.title: Pawnee Nation Mukurtu Portal (Library & Digital Archive Project)
records.access: Free online (some items under cultural protocols)
records.creator: Pawnee Nation, with Washington State University (Mukurtu)
records.contains: Tribe-run online repository on Pawnee history, culture, language and people (treaties, traditional education, etc.). IMLS grants fund locating and digitizing Pawnee materials held by outside archives.
records.why_rating: Tribally curated; Mukurtu lets the Nation set access by cultural protocol.
records.rights: Follow each item's labels and protocols.

project.note: The address did not resolve from this computer on 2026-11-15. A search engine lists mukurtu.pawneenation.org/node/1, 'About the Pawnee Nation Mukurtu Portal'. Try again before listing it for learners.

records.title: Pawnee Nation language lessons 1–3 (PDFs hosted by Northern Oklahoma College)
records.creator: Attributed to the Pawnee Nation by NOC; PDFs are unsigned
records.publisher: Northern Oklahoma College, Cultural Engagement Center
records.contains: Lesson 1 alphabet & basics; Lesson 2 greetings, introductions and kin terms; Lesson 3 basics. Skiri and South Band forms given side by side, in a circumflex spelling (â, î, û, ê, č). Lesson 1 PDF: noc.edu/wp-content/uploads/sites/740/2020/04/pawneelanguage01.pdf
records.why_rating: Practical and dialect-labelled, but unsigned and hosted by a third party; spelling differs from the Parks & Pratt accent system.
records.rights: Educational handouts; ask the Nation before republishing.

project.check: the alphabet the Nation teaches, and which forms are Skiri and which South Band (Lesson 1)

checked.seen: Opened 2026-11-15: Northern Oklahoma College's page says 'The Pawnee Nation also provides the following online lessons in PDF format' and lists Lesson 1: Alphabet and Basics, Lesson 2: Greetings and Introductions, Lesson 3: Basics. Lesson 1 was read in full: 'Vowels (South Band or SB: 8 & Skiri: 6)', "'e,' 'ee' are SB sounds", the consonants p t k č c s h r w ’, long vowels with a circumflex, and Skiri and South Band forms side by side.

project.title: The Nation's lesson handouts
project.says: Three lessons as PDFs, provided by the Pawnee Nation and hosted by Northern Oklahoma College: the alphabet, greetings and introductions, basics. They give Skiri and South Band forms side by side, in the spelling this site calls the learner spelling.

records.title: Pari Pakuru': Introduction to Spoken Pawnee (1979 textbook)
records.creator: Pawnee Cultural Retention Committee
records.publisher: Educational Research Associates, Albuquerque (LC 79-63051); books, cassettes and teacher's guide via IAIA/BIA, Santa Fe
records.contains: Community-produced course. The Pawnee Nation Language Department was still teaching from it (with a CD) in 2006.
records.why_rating: Pawnee-made and long used in tribal classes, but it predates the Parks orthography, and its dialect isn't stated in what I found. Your repo calls it a Skiri “Blue Book”; confirm from the book itself.
records.rights: In copyright (1979); rights likely with the committee/Nation.

project.check: its own account of its two dialects (the alphabet chapter)
project.note: The catalogue asks whether the book is Skiri. The book answers (alphabet chapter, pp. xviii-xxiv): it writes for both dialects in a spelling that follows South Band speakers: 'the South Band e is pronounced by Skidi speakers just as if it were an i'; 'IMPORTANT. The accent marked in this book is that of some South Band speakers'; and it marks a form (SK) or (SB) where the two differ. Copyright page: 'Copyright © 1979 by the Pawnee Indian Tribal Business Council … No part of this book may be reproduced … without permission in writing from the Pawnee Tribal Business Council.' Permission is being asked (2026-11); the owner's decision of 2026-11-15 is to change nothing meanwhile.

records.title: Chaticks si Chaticks (Pawnee Nation newspaper)
records.creator: Pawnee Nation
records.contains: Carries language-department reports, class schedules and Pawnee phrases in notices.
records.why_rating: Official, but language content is occasional and not edited as teaching material.

records.title: Pawnee Nation College
records.creator: Pawnee Nation College
records.contains: Tribal college that has offered Pawnee language courses (Taylor Moore taught there from 2016). Current offerings not verified.
records.why_rating: Tribally connected; couldn't confirm what is taught now.

project.note: No answer on 2026-11-15; what is taught there now is not known. Not listed.

records.title: Pawnee Language Learning (podcast & Substack)
records.creator: Kelli Cedarfield
records.contains: Word-of-the-day episodes plus short grammar, history and culture posts; gives both dialect forms (e.g. âtkahâru' SB / itkahâru' Skiri, “ear”).
records.why_rating: Active and careful about dialect labels, but the author's training and tie to the Nation's program aren't stated in what I could reach. Cross-check words against Parks & Pratt or the IIK database.

project.note: Scored 3 (cross-check) by the catalogue: an independent learner's podcast. Not listed for learners until its words have been checked against the dictionary or the Nation's programme says so.

records.title: “Pâripakûru' with Zach Rice and Taylor Moore” — A Life in Ruins, Ep. 89
records.creator: Zach Rice & Taylor Moore (guests)
records.contains: Two Pawnee Nation citizens and program teachers (OU MAs in linguistic anthropology) on the language program, Northern Caddoan relationships, challenges and goals; show notes list their recommended reading.
records.why_rating: First-hand from the program's teachers; an interview, not a lesson.

checked.seen: Opened 2026-11-15: A Life in Ruins, episode 89, 'Pâripakûru' with Zach Rice and Taylor Moore', 3 January 2022, 1 hr 23 min. The guests are described as citizens of the Pawnee Nation who work with the Pawnee Nation Language Program; the notes recommend A Dictionary of Skiri Pawnee and link the language department's Facebook page and Indiana University's online dictionary. An interview in English about the language, not a lesson. The episode itself was not listened to.

project.title: Two people of the programme talk about the language
project.says: A podcast interview of January 2022, in English, 1 hour 23 minutes, with two citizens of the Pawnee Nation who work with its language programme: how they came to the language and what the programme is working towards. It is a conversation about the language, not a lesson.

records.title: IIK Dictionary Database — Skiri Pawnee (and South Band Pawnee)
records.creator: Douglas R. Parks and colleagues
records.publisher: Indiana University, Institute for Indigenous Knowledge (formerly AISRI)
records.contains: English-keyword search; entries give part of speech, numbered senses, some phonetic forms, and on some entries mp3 audio, example sentences or images. Same portal searches South Band Pawnee and Arikara.
records.why_rating: Built from the same fieldwork as the print dictionary, with native-speaker audio.
records.rights: © Trustees of Indiana University; no open license stated. Ask IIK before bulk reuse.

project.check: how a word sounds (a link, word by word); after permission, a second witness for each dictionary entry
project.note: Searches are plain links (testengltoxsrchNP.php with database=skiri), so a word here can link to its search there. The portal for choosing a dictionary: https://aisri-language-database.webapps.iu.edu/dictsearch/

checked.seen: Opened 2026-11-15: the dictionary search of the Institute for Indigenous Knowledge, Indiana University, over six dictionaries (Arikara, Assiniboine, Dakota, Lakhota, Skiri Pawnee, South Band Pawnee). A search of the Skiri dictionary returned entries with part of speech and, on some, a 'sound file' (mp3). Footer: '©2025, The Trustees of Indiana University'; no licence is stated.

project.title: Indiana University's Skiri dictionary, with sound
project.says: The dictionary this site is made from, online at the Institute for Indigenous Knowledge. Search in English or in Pawnee; some entries have a recording you can play. Type a Pawnee word in plain letters, without the mark for the catch in the throat.

records.title: IIK Northern Caddoan Linguistic Text Corpora
records.creator: Parks's NSF Northern Caddoan Languages Documentation Project (1992–)
records.contains: Skiri: Roaming Scout Collection (ethics narratives first written down by George Dorsey; retranscribed in modern spelling, glossed and analyzed by Parks) and Parks Collection. South Band: Weltfish Collection (in progress). Unicode.
records.why_rating: Analyzed primary texts from the field's main specialist.
records.rights: Cite with the XML date stamp shown on each text; contact Logan Sutton (IIK) about reuse.

project.note: Connected Skiri text analysed by Parks. Wanted for examples and as forms no rule here was fitted to; to ask the institute first, and texts of ceremony are held whatever the answer.

checked.seen: Opened 2026-11-15: 'IIK Northern Caddoan Linguistic Text Corpora'. Skiri Pawnee: Roaming Scout Collection, Parks Collection; South Band Pawnee: Weltfish Collection (in progress). 'Readers should pay attention to that date stamp and include it in any fair-use citations.' Copyright Indiana University; a contact is named for the site.

records.title: Pawnee Language Program curriculum (Pawnee Nation + AISRI)
records.access: Ask Pawnee Nation or IIK (availability unclear)
records.creator: Pawnee Nation & AISRI (Parks; coordinators Adrian Horse Chief, Dollie Gonzales)
records.contains: “Introduction to the Pawnee Language (Skiri Dialect)” textbook, a year of multimedia CD-ROM lessons with native-speaker recordings, a student dictionary and a reader. Skiri recordings by Nora Pratt; South Band by Stacy Matthews and Lynn Rice.
records.why_rating: Co-produced by the Nation and Parks with fluent elders.

project.note: The only beginners' course for Skiri. The project holds no copy (the owner, 2026-11-15). To ask the Nation's Education Department for.

checked.seen: Opened 2026-11-15 at its new address (the spreadsheet's redirects): 'Pawnee Language Program. Language Learning with Technology. A cooperative project between The Pawnee Nation and Indiana University', established 1997: the printed textbook 'Introduction to the Pawnee Language (Skiri Dialect)', a multimedia dictionary, multimedia language lessons on CD-ROM, and the Pawnee Alphabet Book. 'Copies of instructional materials are available from The Pawnee Nation of Oklahoma, Education Department'.

project.title: The Nation's Skiri course
project.says: A beginners' course made from 1997 by the Pawnee Nation with Indiana University: the textbook “Introduction to the Pawnee Language (Skiri Dialect)”, lessons on CD-ROM with a speaker's recordings, and a dictionary with sound. It is not online. The university's page says copies are available from the Nation's Education Department.

records.title: Pawnee Alphabet Book — Writing Pawnee / Rararíhkaruku Paárihkat
records.creator: Pawnee Language Project; intro by Douglas R. Parks; illustrations by Charles Lone Chief
records.contains: Letter-by-letter guide to the Pawnee alphabet, with example words in Skiri and South Band.
records.why_rating: The project's official spelling system.

project.check: the alphabet, and the Skiri and South Band forms of the same word

checked.seen: Read 2026-11-15 at its new address (the spreadsheet's answers 'not found'): 19 pages, made in 2002. Each letter has words in two columns, South Band and Skiri (cáhriks and cáhiks 'person'; iíru' and hiíru' 'grass, hay'; tékskurit and tíkskurit 'near'). It writes a long vowel double and marks the accent, as the dictionary does, and writes c for both the 'patch' and the 'cents' sound; e and ee are in its vowel list with South Band examples only.

project.title: The Pawnee Alphabet Book
project.says: A short guide to the letters (2002) from the Pawnee Nation's language project with Indiana University: each letter with words in South Band and in Skiri, side by side. It writes a long vowel double, as the dictionary does.

records.title: A Dictionary of Skiri Pawnee — Parks & Pratt
records.access: Purchase or library (also e-book via EBSCO / ProQuest)
records.creator: Douglas R. Parks & Lula Nora Pratt
records.publisher: University of Nebraska Press with AISRI, Lincoln
records.contains: About 4,500 entries, English–Skiri and Skiri–English; introduction on sounds, alphabet, sound changes and grammar; appendices of verb conjugations, irregular verb roots and kinship terms. Data from Pratt, 1960s narrative recordings by Harry Mad Bear and Sam Allen, and Roaming Scout's texts. No audio.
records.why_rating: The standard Skiri reference: some 15 years of work between a linguist and a fluent speaker.
records.rights: © University of Nebraska Press. Publishing its full content in a digital tool needs the publisher's permission.

project.note: The catalogue: 'Publishing its full content in a digital tool needs the publisher's permission.' Permission is being asked (2026-11); the owner's decision of 2026-11-15 is to change nothing meanwhile.

records.title: A Grammar of Pawnee — Parks
records.creator: Douglas R. Parks
records.contains: Full reference grammar (xiii + 361 pp.), a revision of Parks's UC Berkeley dissertation. Reviewed by Allan R. Taylor in Language 54(4):969–972 (1978).
records.why_rating: The only full grammar of Pawnee, by its leading specialist.

records.title: Parks, “Pawnee” and “Caddoan Languages” — Handbook of North American Indians, vol. 13 Plains
records.creator: Douglas R. Parks
records.contains: “Pawnee” (pp. 515–547) covers history, bands and culture; “Caddoan Languages” (pp. 80–93) covers the language family.
records.why_rating: Authoritative overview by the leading specialist.

records.title: Weltfish, Caddoan Texts: Pawnee, South Band Dialect
records.creator: Gene Weltfish
records.publisher: G. E. Stechert, New York (Publications of the American Ethnological Society 17)
records.contains: Collection of Pawnee texts with English (x + 251 pp.).
records.why_rating: Primary texts by a Boas-trained linguist; older transcription, and South Band, not Skiri.
records.rights: 1937 US publication: check copyright renewal before reuse.

records.title: Weltfish, “The Vision Story of Fox-Boy, a South Band Pawnee Text”
records.creator: Gene Weltfish
records.contains: A single analyzed South Band narrative (WALS lists it as “The vision story of Fox Bay”).
records.why_rating: Peer-reviewed linguistic text; older transcription.

project.note: Marked by the project on 2026-11-15 as bound up with ceremony, song or sacred narrative. For the Pawnee Nation to say.

records.title: Weltfish, “Morphology of the Pawnee Language” (manuscript)
records.creator: Gene Weltfish
records.publisher: American Philosophical Society, ACLS Collection, Mss.497.3.B63c (item C1.1)
records.contains: 88 pages: an outline of a South Band grammar and a partial description of verb morphology.
records.why_rating: Primary analysis by a trained linguist; unpublished and South Band.

records.title: Rice, “Repurposing the Comparative Method for Pawnee Language and Dialect Revitalization”
records.creator: Zachary Rice
records.contains: Sets up sound correspondences between Skiri, South Band and Arikara, and uses them to propose new Pawnee words from Arikara forms; extensive appendices.
records.why_rating: By a Pawnee citizen and program teacher, but MA-level, and the new words are proposals, not attested forms.

project.check: the sound correspondences between Skiri and South Band (not read yet)
project.note: Its new words are proposals from Arikara forms, not attested Pawnee: never to be copied in.

records.title: Moore, “Language Revitalization Through Pawnee Music”
records.creator: Taylor Moore
records.contains: Pawnee hymns as a teaching tool and their recent revival.
records.why_rating: The author is now the Pawnee Nation's Language Manager and an IIK research associate; MA-level.

records.title: Smithsonian NAA MS 2520 — The Ceremonies of the Pawnee (manuscript)
records.creator: James R. Murie; ed. Clark Wissler; phonetic texts revised and translated by Gene Weltfish
records.contains: 2,275 pages, 18 photographs and 27 sketches; includes Murie's 1911 Pawnee star chart with his explanatory letter.
records.why_rating: Primary documentation by a fluent Skiri Pawnee scholar.
records.rights: Ceremonial content: culturally sensitive; consult the Nation.

records.title: Smithsonian NAA MS 1788 — Ceremonial Songs of the Pawnee
records.creator: Helen H. Roberts & James R. Murie
records.contains: 624 pages of song transcriptions and musical analysis, with Murie's notes on the songs and their composers; companion to MS 2520 (a BAE file mentions 95 song recordings).
records.why_rating: Primary, with a fluent Pawnee collaborator.

records.title: Murie, ed. Parks — Ceremonies of the Pawnee, Part I: The Skiri; Part II: The South Bands
records.creator: James R. Murie; edited by Douglas R. Parks
records.publisher: Smithsonian Institution Press (Smithsonian Contributions to Anthropology 27)
records.contains: Parks's edition of the MS 2520 manuscript, which had sat in the BAE archives since 1921.
records.why_rating: Primary content edited by the leading Pawnee linguist.
records.rights: Smithsonian publication; check the item's license.

records.title: Fletcher, The Hako: A Pawnee Ceremony
records.creator: Alice C. Fletcher, assisted by James R. Murie; music by Edwin S. Tracy
records.publisher: Bureau of American Ethnology, 22nd Annual Report pt. 2 (UNP reprint 1996)
records.contains: The Chawi band's calumet ceremony, with the text and music of every song, translations, and the ritual leader Tahirussawichi's explanations.
records.why_rating: Detailed primary record, but early transcription and a South Band ceremony.
records.rights: Public domain (“No Copyright – United States”). Ceremonial content: consult the Nation.

records.title: Densmore, Pawnee Music (BAE Bulletin 93)
records.creator: Frances Densmore
records.contains: Songs (including hand-game and Ghost Dance songs) with notes; some song words.
records.why_rating: Careful, but music-focused, with limited language data.

records.title: APS — Douglas Parks, Pawnee Texts (1966 audio), Mss.Rec.67
records.creator: Douglas R. Parks; speakers Sam Allen, Harry Cummings, Phillip Jim
records.contains: 11 narratives told in Pawnee only, recorded in Pawnee, OK; 4 h 56 min, digitized.
records.why_rating: Fluent-speaker audio recorded by Parks.
records.rights: APS open access for non-commercial, scholarly and educational use.

project.note: Two Skiri narratives among eleven. The archive's site turns automated clients away, so the entry was not seen. To ask about after the institute and the Nation have answered.

records.title: APS — Mary R. Haas Papers, Pawnee materials
records.creator: Mary R. Haas, with Mark Evarts
records.contains: Linguistics and folklore material recorded with Mark Evarts (also Weltfish's Skiri collaborator).
records.why_rating: Major linguist; I did not see the item itself.

records.title: APS — James M. Crawford Papers, Pawnee materials
records.creator: James M. Crawford
records.contains: Pawnee materials in a linguist's papers; catalogued as English-language.
records.why_rating: Credible collector, but contents not reviewed and probably slight.

records.title: APS — Floyd G. Lounsbury Papers, Pawnee kinship materials
records.creator: Floyd G. Lounsbury
records.contains: Annotated offprint of Lounsbury's analysis of Pawnee kinship usage, published in Language, with related notes.
records.why_rating: Peer-reviewed semantic analysis of kin terms.
records.rights: In copyright (journal); APS permissions for notes.

records.title: Newberry Library — Gene Weltfish Pawnee field notes
records.creator: Gene Weltfish, with Mark Evarts and other elders
records.contains: 11 volumes reconstructing a Skidi village's year in 1867 (hunts, harvest, households, doctoring, ceremonies and dances). Flagged as culturally sensitive.
records.why_rating: Primary, but ethnographic rather than linguistic.
records.rights: Copyright may rest with Weltfish's heirs; Newberry permission to reproduce.

records.title: Field Museum — George A. Dorsey & James R. Murie notes and manuscripts
records.creator: George A. Dorsey & James R. Murie
records.publisher: Field Museum, Department of Anthropology archives
records.contains: Notes and manuscripts on Pawnee and Arikara society and religion, including Murie's largely unpublished “Pawnee Ethnographic and Linguistic Notes”; finding aid funded by Save America's Treasures.
records.why_rating: Primary material from a fluent Skiri scholar.
records.rights: Field Museum permissions; consult the Nation on ceremonial content.

records.title: IU Archives of Traditional Music — Native North American recordings
records.access: Recordings on request; catalog free (CC BY-NC-ND)
records.creator: Various collectors (incl. George A. Dorsey)
records.contains: Holds early cylinder recordings, including those Dorsey made for the Field Museum; Dorothy Sara Lee's catalog of the Native American holdings is open access.
records.why_rating: Major archive; specific Pawnee items still need locating in the catalog.

project.note: Marked by the project on 2026-11-15 as bound up with ceremony, song or sacred narrative. For the Pawnee Nation to say.

records.title: Library of Congress American Folklife Center — cylinders & LP AFS L25
records.creator: Frances Densmore, Alice Fletcher and others
records.publisher: Library of Congress, American Folklife Center
records.contains: About 10,000 wax cylinders of Native song and speech; the Federal Cylinder Project returns copies to tribes. Densmore's Pawnee songs were issued on LP AFS L25 with Northern Ute songs (liner notes at link).
records.why_rating: National archive; song more than speech.

records.title: OU Western History Collections — Doris Duke American Indian Oral History Collection
records.creator: OU interviewers with Pawnee elders
records.contains: 600+ interviews with Native elders across Oklahoma, including Pawnee ones (e.g. Pawnee Doctor Dance, religion of the Pawnees).
records.why_rating: Primary community voices; language content incidental.

project.note: Marked by the project on 2026-11-15 as bound up with ceremony, song or sacred narrative. For the Pawnee Nation to say.

records.title: Dorsey, Traditions of the Skidi Pawnee
records.creator: George A. Dorsey (collected with James R. Murie)
records.publisher: Memoirs of the American Folk-Lore Society 8
records.contains: Skiri myths and tales in English translation.
records.why_rating: Primary narrative collection; very little Pawnee-language text.

project.note: Marked by the project on 2026-11-15 as bound up with ceremony, song or sacred narrative. For the Pawnee Nation to say.

records.title: Dorsey, The Pawnee Mythology (Part I)
records.creator: George A. Dorsey
records.contains: Tales tagged as Chaui, Kitkehahki, Skidi or Pitahauirat.
records.why_rating: Primary narrative collection; English only.

project.note: Marked by the project on 2026-11-15 as bound up with ceremony, song or sacred narrative. For the Pawnee Nation to say.

records.title: Dorsey & Murie, Notes on Skidi Pawnee Society
records.creator: George A. Dorsey & James R. Murie; prepared by Alexander Spoehr
records.contains: Community organization, kinship and status, life cycle; Spoehr marks where notes disagree with published data.
records.why_rating: Primary field notes; spellings predate Parks.
records.rights: Freely posted on BHL; check terms.

records.title: Murie, Pawnee Indian Societies
records.creator: James R. Murie
records.publisher: American Museum of Natural History, Anthropological Papers 11(7)
records.contains: Monograph on Pawnee societies (military, hunt, shamanistic and others), by a Skiri Pawnee scholar.
records.why_rating: Primary; older spelling.

project.note: Marked by the project on 2026-11-15 as bound up with ceremony, song or sacred narrative. For the Pawnee Nation to say.

records.title: Grinnell, Pawnee Hero Stories and Folk-Tales (with Dunbar's “The Pawnee Language”)
records.creator: George Bird Grinnell; language chapter by John B. Dunbar
records.contains: Hero stories and folk-tales; the 1893 edition adds Dunbar's chapter on the Pawnee language. Check that the copy you open includes it.
records.why_rating: Useful history, but 19th-century outsider spellings; not reliable for pronunciation.

records.title: Hayden, “Brief Notes on the Pawnee, Winnebago, and Omaha Languages”
records.creator: F. V. Hayden
records.publisher: Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 10(78): 389–421
records.contains: Early vocabulary notes on three languages.
records.why_rating: Amateur ad hoc spelling; historical interest only.

records.title: Lesser, The Pawnee Ghost Dance Hand Game
records.dialect: Both (separate South Band and Skiri chapters)
records.creator: Alexander Lesser
records.contains: 19th-century history, the Ghost Dance among the Pawnee, and the old and Ghost Dance hand games, band by band.
records.why_rating: Scholarly primary fieldwork; not a language study.

records.title: Weltfish, The Lost Universe: Pawnee Life and Culture
records.creator: Gene Weltfish
records.publisher: Basic Books 1965; University of Nebraska Press 1977
records.contains: Year-in-the-life reconstruction of Skidi Pawnee culture; Pawnee terms appear throughout.
records.why_rating: Widely regarded as the authoritative Pawnee ethnography; not a language text.

project.note: Marked by the project on 2026-11-15 as bound up with ceremony, song or sacred narrative. For the Pawnee Nation to say.

records.title: Chamberlain, When Stars Came Down to Earth (Skidi cosmology)
records.creator: Von Del Chamberlain
records.contains: Skidi cosmology with an annotated list of named sky objects, drawing on Murie's journals. Parks reviewed it in “Interpreting Pawnee Star Lore: Science or Myth?”
records.why_rating: Strong on astronomy; for the Pawnee words, check spellings against Parks & Pratt.

records.title: Linton, Field Museum leaflets on Skidi ceremonies
records.creator: Ralph Linton
records.contains: “The Sacrifice to the Morning Star by the Skidi Pawnee” (1922) and “Purification of the Sacred Bundles” (1923).
records.why_rating: Largely copied from Dorsey/Murie field notes without crediting Murie; go to the originals.

records.title: UBC RelLex Knowledgebase — entry on A Dictionary of Skiri Pawnee
records.creator: UBC Relational Lexicography project
records.contains: Structured description of the dictionary's layout and features (bidirectional; no audio, images or example phrases) and the speakers and community contributors it credits.
records.why_rating: Careful academic profile; describes the source, adds no language data.

records.title: Glottolog — Pawnee (pawn1254)
records.creator: Glottolog editors
records.contains: Classification, endangerment status and a searchable bibliography of Pawnee references; links to OLAC, ELP, WALS and Grambank.
records.why_rating: Best place to find more literature; it describes sources rather than holding language data.

records.title: OLAC — Pawnee [paw] archive records
records.creator: Open Language Archives Community
records.contains: Pulls together catalog records of Pawnee holdings from participating archives (e.g. APS digital records).
records.why_rating: Reliable catalog for finding archival items.

records.title: Endangered Languages Project — Pawnee
records.creator: ELP / user contributors
records.contains: Status data (1–9 speakers, most South Band, per its source), bibliography entries, and an uploaded video on the Pawnee alphabet.
records.why_rating: Status data is sourced; uploads vary in quality.

records.title: WALS — Pawnee
records.creator: WALS editors
records.contains: Coded grammatical features drawing on Parks 1976 and Weltfish 1936/1937.
records.why_rating: Scholarly coding, but second-hand from the grammars.

records.title: ASJP — Pawnee word list
records.creator: ASJP project
records.contains: Short basic-vocabulary list taken from Parks & Pratt, written in ASJP's simplified code.
records.why_rating: Accurate source, but the simplified transcription drops detail.

records.title: Ethnologue — Pawnee [paw]
records.creator: SIL International
records.contains: Language profile and status.
records.why_rating: Standard reference, but status figures for Pawnee vary across sources.

records.title: Wikipedia — Pawnee language
records.creator: Wikipedia editors
records.contains: Overview, phonology, alphabets and useful links.
records.why_rating: Handy for links, but inconsistent: says Skiri died out in 2001 while citing speaker counts, and its phonology describes only South Band.

records.title: Omniglot — Pawnee
records.creator: Simon Ager, with contributors
records.contains: Alphabet and pronunciation table, a sample Skiri text taken from the AISRI corpus, and links.
records.why_rating: Draws on AISRI, but secondary, and its “about 100 speakers” is out of date.

records.title: Native Languages of the Americas — Pawnee word lists
records.creator: Native Languages of the Americas
records.contains: Small themed word lists (e.g. animals) and a pronunciation guide.
records.why_rating: No sources or dialect given; not updated since 2015.

records.title: Wiktionary — Pawnee
records.creator: Wiktionary editors
records.contains: A handful of Pawnee entries.
records.why_rating: Very few entries, crowd-edited.

records.title: San Juan College research guide — Pawnee / pâri pakûru'
records.creator: San Juan College Library
records.contains: Librarian-made overview linking the Nation's YouTube classes, the Pâripakûru' Facebook page and the podcast.
records.why_rating: Good pointer list; secondary.

records.title: The Revenant (2015 film)
records.creator: Dialogue prepared with Indiana University linguists
records.contains: Feature film with spoken Pawnee lines.
records.why_rating: Prepared by IU linguists, but scripted lines, not teaching material.
